primary_outcome_name: 6-minute walking distance (6MWD), as measure of functional exercise capacity
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: 6-minute walking test (6MWT), performed per European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society guidelines; outcome recorded as 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) in metres
primary_timepoint: post-treatment, 6 weeks after baseline (~42.9 days on average)
population_detail: Formerly hospitalised COVID-19 survivors, aged 18-75 years, with remaining moderate dyspnoea (mMRC score 2-3) after discharge from one of three hospitals in Jiangsu and Hubei provinces, China; recruited April-May 2020.

published_estimate.quote: The mean 6MWD in the control group increased by 17.1 m (SD 63.9) from baseline to post-treatment assessment, whereas 6MWD in the TERECO group improved by 80.2 m (SD 74.7). The adjusted between-group difference in change in 6MWD from baseline (treatment effect) was 65.45 m (95% CI 43.8 to 87.1; p<0.001). [Results, 'Primary outcome' section, p.700; consistent with Table 2, p.701: 6MWD (m), Post-treatment (6 weeks): 65.45 (43.80 to 87.10), P<0.001]

B_covariate_list: Study centre (fixed effect; = randomisation stratification factor, 'stratified by hospital'). Baseline value itself is not entered as a classic regression covariate but is handled via constrained longitudinal data analysis (cLDA): a linear mixed model with equality constraint on baseline means across arms, which the authors explicitly describe as 'analogous to analysis of covariance'.
data_availability_statement: Data availability statement: Anonymised patient-level data on which the analysis, results and conclusions reported in this paper are based are available as Dryad dataset. Reinhardt, Jan D. (2021), Telerehabilitation program for COVID-19 survivors (TERECO) - randomized controlled trial, Dryad, Dataset, https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.59zw3r27n

registry_check.issues: arm coding is reversed relative to the registry.csv notation: registry states arm_var=group_randomized, arm_control=1, but in the deposited data (TERECO_Public_Data_wide.csv) group_randomized=1 has baseline _6MWD1 mean 514.52 (SD 82.17, n=59) and group_randomized=2 has mean 499.98 (SD 92.63, n=60) -- these match the paper's Table 1 TERECO/intervention (n=59, mean 514.52, SD 82.87) and control (n=60, mean 499.98, SD 93.41) groups respectively. Also, all 7 missing post-treatment 6MWD values (_6MWD2) are in group_randomized=1, consistent with dropout being reported for the TERECO group in the paper. Conclusion: group_randomized=1 is TERECO/intervention, group_randomized=2 is control -- i.e. arm_control should be 2, not 1, as currently set in registry.csv. Outcome variables (X_6MWD1=baseline, X_6MWD2=post-treatment) correctly match the paper's declared primary outcome and timepoint. The registry note '7 fehlend post' is confirmed exactly (7 missing _6MWD2 values, all in the TERECO arm; n=119 baseline-analysed minus 7 = 112 = 60 control + 52 TERECO analysed post-treatment, matching Table 2).

analysis_method_quote: Statistical analysis: All analyses were performed with STATA V.14.0. Main analyses were conducted on intention-to-treat (ITT) basis without imputations. Statistical significance was set at alpha=5% with two-sided tests. Data were assumed to be missing at random (MAR) with missing values depending on observed model parameters. This assumption was tested with sensitivity analysis. [...] The 6MWD was evaluated with constrained longitudinal data analysis, that is a linear mixed effects model that imposed an equality constraint on baseline means. Analogous to analysis of covariance, such equality constraint is imposed to counteract regression to the mean [...]. The model was adjusted for centre (fixed effect) and dependence of longitudinal observations within study participants was modelled with a random intercept. Parameters for interaction terms between time and treatment represent the estimated treatment effects at post-treatment and follow-up, and are reported with 95% CIs. All secondary outcomes apart from mMRC-dyspnoea were analysed analogously. (p.699-700, 'Statistical analysis' section)
notes: Primary outcome is explicitly declared under a dedicated 'Primary outcome' heading in Methods (p.698-699) and matches the Abstract ('Primary outcome was 6 min walking distance (6MWD) in metres'); the actual trial-registry record text is not reproduced in the paper (only the registration number ChiCTR2000031834 and a protocol URL are given), so 'registration' could not be verified directly from the paper text -- coded as 'methods_first_named' on that basis. Note that 6MWD was also measured at follow-up (~28 weeks), but that follow-up assessment is explicitly presented under 'Secondary outcomes' in Methods (p.699: 'The 6MWD at follow-up was assessed as described in the previous section') -- so only the post-treatment (6-week) 6MWD contrast is the primary analysis; the follow-up 6MWD estimate (68.62 m, 95% CI 46.39-90.85, p<0.001) is technically a secondary-outcome estimate despite sharing the same outcome variable. n_randomised=120 (61 allocated control, 59 TERECO per Abstract); n_analysed_primary=119 is the ITT population with baseline data used in the primary mixed model (control n=60, TERECO n=59; one control patient excluded post-randomisation as ineligible/mistakenly randomised) -- this matches Table 3's sensitivity-analysis header 'ITT, primary analysis (n=119, nint=59, nobs=336)'. A further, smaller complete-case count applies specifically to the post-treatment 6MWD value: n=112 (control=60, TERECO=52); the mixed model itself, however, uses all available observations from all n=119 (direct-likelihood/MMRM-type approach under ITT, no imputation), not just the post-treatment completers. Exact p-value for the primary contrast is reported only as 'p<0.001' (not a specific numeric value), hence published_estimate.p is left null rather than approximated. published_group_stats.followup_mean/sd are null because Table 2 reports only mean CHANGE from baseline ± SD (control 17.09±63.94 m; TERECO 80.20±74.66 m at post-treatment, on the post-treatment-completer subset n=60/52), not absolute post-treatment 6MWD levels; computing absolute follow-up means from baseline+change would require the same subset for both, which is not directly given, so no value was invented. journal_requires_data_sharing coded 'yes' based on the presence of a mandatory-style structured 'Data availability statement' section (BMJ/Thorax house style) with actual open deposition, not from an explicit statement of journal policy within the paper text. Sensitivity analyses (per-protocol, MAR multiple imputation, CIR/non-MAR multiple imputation, TOS-adjusted post hoc model) are prespecified/post hoc alternatives to the ITT primary analysis and are reported in Table 3, but are not the published primary estimate.
